translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every choice of types P, D, E, R, every record t of type S3 P D E R, and every r in R, let Q be the set of p in P for which some d in t.c1(p) has t.c3(d) = r. For each p in P, let U(p) be the union of t.c2(d) over all d in t.c1(p), not just those with t.c3(d) = r. If there exist a function S from Q to Q and a p in Q such that U(p) and U(S(p)) are disjoint, then for every o in D, if o belongs to t.c1(q) for some q in P and t.c3(o) = r, then t.c4(t.c3(o)) does not belong to t.c2(o). The hypothesis requires disjointness only for the chosen p and its image, and does not require S(p) to differ from p. The conclusion is not restricted to objects belonging to t.c1(p) or t.c1(S(p)).

divergences.description: The source concludes `∃ o ∈ t.D17, t.c3 o = r ∧ t.D18 o`: at least one dataset that can arise with inference content `r` gives a falsification. The TARGET instead requires falsification at every such dataset. The inferred value can agree with a prediction on one side of the substitution while being excluded on the other, so disjointness does not justify the universal conclusion.

judgement.summary: The substitution hypothesis matches Definition 3.1, but the TARGET changes the lemmas’ conclusion from “some dataset” to “every dataset” with the specified inference content.
